vulnerability_analysis: The Advisory contract has a constructor that sets critical parameters (token address, claimPeriod, subsequentClaim) only once during deployment. If deployed with malicious parameters (claimPeriod = 1, subsequentClaim = 100e18), and using a token contract controlled by the attacker, the attacker (as owner/deployer) can add themselves as a distribution wallet and immediately claim 100% of their allocated balance due to the claim formula: claimAmount = (balance * (subsequentClaim * totDays)) / 100e18. With claimPeriod = 1 second and subsequentClaim = 100e18, after 1 second, totDays = 1, making claimAmount = balance * 100e18 / 100e18 = balance (100%).
attack_strategy: 1. Deploy a malicious ERC20 token controlled by attacker. 2. Deploy Advisory contract with malicious parameters (token = malicious token, claimPeriod = 1, subsequentClaim = 100e18). 3. Mint tokens to Advisory contract. 4. As owner (attacker), add attacker address as distribution wallet with large balance. 5. Wait 1 second (warp time). 6. Call claim() to drain all tokens.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy MockBEP20 token contract. 2. Deploy Advisory contract with malicious parameters. 3. Mint tokens to Advisory contract using deal() cheatcode. 4. Call addDistributionWallet() as owner to add attacker with large balance. 5. Warp time forward by 1 second. 6. Call claim() to get all tokens. 7. Verify attacker token balance increased.
